title: The Bond Market Sell-Off Is Appearing in Earnings Reports
author: Motley Fool Staff
description: Rising bond yields at 20-year highs are impacting corporate earnings and stock performance. Klarna reported strong operational metrics but cut guidance due to softer consumer spending in Germany, causing a 21% stock decline. Home Depot beat expectations despite a frozen housing market but showed limited growth. The higher interest rate environment is pressuring companies reliant on consumer spending and capital-intensive AI buildouts, with hyperscaler capex expected to reach $1.2 trillion next year, increasingly funded by debt.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock fell 21% despite strong operational metrics (27% revenue growth, improved credit quality) due to substantial guidance cuts attributed to currency headwinds and reduced expectations from Germany. Management changes (CFO and CMO departing) and concerns about consumer spending in higher rate environment added to weakness.

Beat earnings expectations in a frozen housing market, showing resilience with 1.7% comp store sales growth (accelerating from prior quarter). However, growth remains below inflation, big projects remain on hold, and stock is up only 5% over five years. Company faces headwinds from higher interest rates suppressing housing demand.

Reported first quarter of negative free cash flow since going public due to massive AI capex spending. Rising debt funding needs and higher interest rates increase cost of capital for continued AI infrastructure buildout.

title: C Nears China Brokerage License: Can Onshore Expansion Boost Growth?
author: Na
description: Citigroup is on track to receive final regulatory approval for a wholly owned China brokerage business by September 2026. The platform will offer A-share brokerage, underwriting, research, and principal trading services, enabling the bank to deepen client relationships and increase its investment-banking wallet share above 6%. This expansion aligns with Citigroup's OneCiti strategy and repositioning toward institutional banking in China following the sale of its consumer banking business to HSBC in 2024.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Moving closer to regulatory approval for a wholly owned China brokerage business, which represents a significant expansion opportunity. The new platform will enable deeper client relationships, access to domestic capital markets, and support the bank's goal of increasing investment-banking wallet share from 4.7% to over 6%.

title: Capital Markets Momentum Fades: What it Means for Big Banks in Q3
author: Na
description: U.S. banks enter Q3 2026 with supportive lending conditions but face mixed capital markets trends. Investment banking volumes declined 6% YoY in July due to weak debt markets, though M&A and equity underwriting showed strength. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley face greater sensitivity to capital markets weakness, while diversified banks like JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citigroup benefit from broader revenue streams including loan and deposit growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Most sensitive to weaker capital markets conditions. While benefits from M&A and equity underwriting strength, weakness in debt capital markets could offset gains and moderate investment banking revenue growth.

title: Earnings Growth & Price Strength Make Goldman Sachs (GS) a Stock to Watch
author: Zacks.Com
description: Goldman Sachs (GS) has been highlighted as a strong investment opportunity due to positive earnings growth and price momentum. The company, added to the Zacks Focus List in July 2018, has seen shares increase 357.84% since then. Seven analysts revised earnings estimates higher in the last 60 days, with the consensus estimate increasing to $68.89, and GS is rated #1 (Strong Buy) on the Zacks Rank with expected earnings growth of 34.2% for the current fiscal year.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: GS receives a positive sentiment due to multiple bullish indicators: (1) Seven analysts revised earnings estimates higher in the last 60 days, (2) Zacks Consensus Estimate increased by $8.39 to $68.89, (3) Company holds #1 (Strong Buy) rating on Zacks Rank, (4) Expected earnings growth of 34.2% for current fiscal year, (5) Average earnings surprise of 20.4%, and (6) Strong historical performance with 357.84% share price increase since Focus List addition in July 2018.

title: Should State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) Be on Your Investing Radar?
author: Zacks.Com
description: The State Street SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) is highlighted as a strong option for investors seeking large-cap value exposure. With $45.92 billion in assets, a low 0.16% expense ratio, and a Zacks ETF Rank of 1 (Strong Buy), DIA has gained 12.02% year-to-date and 18.46% over the past year. The ETF holds 31 blue-chip stocks with heavy exposure to Financials (27.5%), led by holdings in Goldman Sachs, Caterpillar, and Microsoft.
